Gov. JB Pritzker speaks at the signing of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Safety Measures Act in the Loop July 6.

Gov. JB Pritzker is convening a panel of experts to advise state officials on the potential threats of artificial intelligence as a growing number of industry leaders warn the burgeoning, self-improving technology could spell doomsday for humanity if left unchecked.

The Democratic governor signed an executive order Tuesday establishing the Illinois Artificial Intelligence Cabinet to assess “the various risks posed by Al to the safety of Illinois residents and the critical infrastructure residents rely on.”

Pritzker will name his AI Cabinet members “in the coming weeks” to work alongside numerous state agency leaders, including from the Department of Innovation and Technology, the Department of Public Health and the Illinois Emergency Management Agency.

They’re expected to come from backgrounds in academia, law, ethics and governance, and provide recommendations on potential public safety threats, protecting public assets and evaluating possible regulations, according to Pritzker’s office.

His order comes in the wake of former Anthropic AI researcher Jacob Coxon’s media blitz this month warning that aggressive industry development in the absence of federal regulation “could kill us all by the end of the decade.”
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Meta chairman Mark Zuckerberg and other AI executives have emphasized the need for broader safety measures.

“Artificial Intelligence has enormous potential to transform our everyday lives, but when experts and industry leaders sound the alarm bell, urge us to slow down, and ask for guardrails, we should listen,” Pritzker said in a statement.
In July, Pritzker signed a package of state-level AI regulations into law that mark some of the most stringent in the nation, requiring frontier developers to submit to annual independent audits.
Pritzker, who has done little to quell speculation about his own presidential ambitions, has blasted President Donald Trump for his administration’s lax approach to AI regulation.

“Illinois has already enacted nation-leading laws that hold Big Tech accountable and today I’m taking executive action to keep this a priority,” Pritzker said. “Congress and the White House need to treat AI risks with urgency, but in the meantime, Illinois won’t wait because it is our foremost responsibility to prepare and protect Illinoisans.”

University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign Chancellor Charles Isbell said in a statement that his institution is “eager to help the state navigate the current challenges and opportunities that AI brings.”

“As a land-grant institution, we are committed to innovation for the public good and to developing human-centered AI that protects privacy, reduces bias, strengthens democratic institutions, uses energy wisely, and creates value for workers, companies and communities,” Isbell said.

sources.title: Pritzker establishes AI cabinet amid calls for greater regulation - NPR Illinois
passages: Pritzker signed an executive order on Tuesday to establish an AI Cabinet made up of experts and representatives from several state agencies.

The unpaid group, which will formulate policy proposals through 2027, will analyze and assess “the various risks posed by AI to the safety of Illinois residents and the critical infrastructure residents rely on.”

Pritzker signed Senate Bill 315 in July, also known as the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act , which increases transparency and accountability requirements for the largest artificial intelligence models — those that generate more than $500 million in annual revenue and are trained using massive computing power.

It establishes new reporting standards for the possibility that the AI model could be used for large-scale harm, such as by helping create a chemical, biological or nuclear weapon or committing cyber-attacks.

Gov. JB Pritzker speaks at the signing of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Safety Measures Act in the Loop July 6.

Gov. JB Pritzker is convening a panel of experts to advise state officials on the potential threats of artificial intelligence as a growing number of industry leaders warn the burgeoning, self-improving technology could spell doomsday for humanity if left unchecked.

The Democratic governor signed an executive order Tuesday establishing the Illinois Artificial Intelligence Cabinet to assess “the various risks posed by Al to the safety of Illinois residents and the critical infrastructure residents rely on.”

Pritzker will name his AI Cabinet members “in the coming weeks” to work alongside numerous state agency leaders, including from the Department of Innovation and Technology, the Department of Public Health and the Illinois Emergency Management Agency.

They’re expected to come from backgrounds in academia, law, ethics and governance, and provide recommendations on potential public safety threats, protecting public assets and evaluating possible regulations, according to Pritzker’s office.

His order comes in the wake of former Anthropic AI researcher Jacob Coxon’s media blitz this month warning that aggressive industry development in the absence of federal regulation “could kill us all by the end of the decade.”
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Meta chairman Mark Zuckerberg and other AI executives have emphasized the need for broader safety measures.

“Artificial Intelligence has enormous potential to transform our everyday lives, but when experts and industry leaders sound the alarm bell, urge us to slow down, and ask for guardrails, we should listen,” Pritzker said in a statement.
In July, Pritzker signed a package of state-level AI regulations into law that mark some of the most stringent in the nation, requiring frontier developers to submit to annual independent audits.
Pritzker, who has done little to quell speculation about his own presidential ambitions, has blasted President Donald Trump for his administration’s lax approach to AI regulation.

“Illinois has already enacted nation-leading laws that hold Big Tech accountable and today I’m taking executive action to keep this a priority,” Pritzker said. “Congress and the White House need to treat AI risks with urgency, but in the meantime, Illinois won’t wait because it is our foremost responsibility to prepare and protect Illinoisans.”

University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign Chancellor Charles Isbell said in a statement that his institution is “eager to help the state navigate the current challenges and opportunities that AI brings.”

“As a land-grant institution, we are committed to innovation for the public good and to developing human-centered AI that protects privacy, reduces bias, strengthens democratic institutions, uses energy wisely, and creates value for workers, companies and communities,” Isbell said.

extraction.body: SPRINGFIELD — Gov. JB Pritzker is setting up a new group within state government to explore more regulations for artificial intelligence as calls grow across the country for new restrictions. Pritzker signed an executive order on Tuesday to establish an AI Cabinet made up of experts and representatives from several state agencies. The unpaid group, which will formulate policy proposals through 2027, will analyze and assess “the various risks posed by AI to the safety of Illinois residents and the critical infrastructure residents rely on.” It’s the latest move by Illinois to tackle state-focused AI regulation as the federal government continues to take a hands-off approach , even as industry insiders sound the alarm on the technology’s capabilities. A former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher alleged in an explosive social media post earlier this month that AI companies are building a tool that could become “out of control” and pose a threat to human existence by 2030. “Artificial Intelligence has enormous potential to transform our everyday lives, but when experts and industry leaders sound the alarm bell, urge us to slow down, and ask for guardrails, we should listen,” Pritzker said in a statement. The cabinet will formulate policies and procedures to protect Illinois residents and public assets like water systems, education and information systems from threats posed by AI. It will also analyze “emerging AI incidents and share lessons learned” from them. The advisory group will also make policy recommendations on risk management and assess the feasibility, timeframe and any other challenges for implementing them. The cabinet will consider regulations tying data center incentives or operational approval to a company’s ability to meet safety, accountability and transparency standards. It will also look into addressing strain on the energy grid from data centers, evaluating how state procurement and contracting practices can incorporate AI safety and accountability measures, and assessing if existing legal options are good enough to hold AI companies that cause harm accountable. Illinois lawmakers have already taken steps to regulate AI. Pritzker signed Senate Bill 315 in July, also known as the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act , which increases transparency and accountability requirements for the largest artificial intelligence models — those that generate more than $500 million in annual revenue and are trained using massive computing power. It establishes new reporting standards for the possibility that the AI model could be used for large-scale harm, such as by helping create a chemical, biological or nuclear weapon or committing cyber-attacks. It also made Illinois the first state to require annual audits of AI. The law takes effect in 2028. Since the whistleblower came forward earlier this month, Pritzker has been aggressively calling on Congress to step in. “It should be among the top priorities, but don't misunderstand, it is dangerous and it's dangerous on the level of nuclear weapons,” Pritzker said on ABC’s Sunday morning news show . “So that's why it needs to be an international endeavor. Pritzker has urged Congress to immediately begin holding hearings on AI safety and impose national standards. sources.title: OpenAI’s Altman and Anthropic’s Amodei address UN security council - theguardian.com
passages: Sam Altman of OpenAI and Dario Amodei of Anthropic, heads of two of the world’s largest artificial intelligence companies, addressed the United Nations security council on Wednesday in separate briefings on AI safety.
Altman and Amodei spoke as their companies face increasing scrutiny over the safety of their products.
Public alarm over AI has grown in response to warnings from Anthropic researchers earlier this month that the technology could destroy humanity within the decade.
He advocated for governments to come together to build a future where AI is guided by democratic institutions, rather than one where people feel like the technology is “something being done to them”.
Earlier, Amodei called for a slowdown in AI development, which was supported by OpenAI , Google and Elon Musk.

Altman argued there was instead a “middle path” through the safety debate that should be based on three principles: AI systems must remain under human control; AI must benefit people, from helping doctors treat patients to boosting entrepreneurs; and the technology must “empower people individually”.

While Altman steered his address away from engaging with the warnings of existential risk that have made headlines this month, Amodei reiterated his concerns about developers losing control of AI while also framing his company as an industry leader on safety.
“If managed poorly, I even believe that AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole,” Amodei said.
“At Anthropic, we believe we have the best track record in the industry for preventing these risks”.
Their companies are also jockeying for the lead in the AI race, with both eyeing potentially record-setting initial public offerings that would value each at more than $1.5tn.
“We have a choice in front of us,” Altman told the council.
“AI can either be more like a new renaissance of creativity and discovery, or more like a new industrial revolution of upheaval and disarray.”
“If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone.
They must be shaped through democratic processes and by governments accountable to the people that they serve,” Altman said.

extraction.body: Heads of two of the world’s largest artificial intelligence companies give separate briefings on AI safety Sam Altman of OpenAI and Dario Amodei of Anthropic, heads of two of the world’s largest artificial intelligence companies, addressed the United Nations security council on Wednesday in separate briefings on AI safety. “We have a choice in front of us,” Altman told the council. “AI can either be more like a new renaissance of creativity and discovery, or more like a new industrial revolution of upheaval and disarray.” Altman and Amodei spoke as their companies face increasing scrutiny over the safety of their products. Public alarm over AI has grown in response to warnings from Anthropic researchers earlier this month that the technology could destroy humanity within the decade. Leaders of AI companies, including Altman and Amodei, have since called for a slowdown on advancing AI and more international cooperation on the technology’s safety standards. Altman, who sat at the corner of the security council’s horseshoe-shaped table and spoke for about 10 minutes, touted AI’s benefits to productivity while also warning of its potential abuses. He advocated for governments to come together to build a future where AI is guided by democratic institutions, rather than one where people feel like the technology is “something being done to them”. “If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone. They must be shaped through democratic processes and by governments accountable to the people that they serve,” Altman said. The OpenAI CEO’s speech contrasted with some of his company’s lobbying efforts and the political action committee of its president, Greg Brockman. The pro-AI Leading the Future PAC has accrued more than $100m and spent millions targeting candidates who support stronger regulation on the AI industry. Altman’s speech also nodded to some of the concerns from Anthropic researchers about AI’s existential risk, warning the council against falling into “doomerism”. Altman argued there was instead a “middle path” through the safety debate that should be based on three principles: AI systems must remain under human control; AI must benefit people, from helping doctors treat patients to boosting entrepreneurs; and the technology must “empower people individually”. Amodei, who addressed the council via video call, repeated many of the points that he made in a 12 September blog post that called for increased global cooperation and oversight of AI. He advocated for several forms of international agreements, including a ban on using AI to develop biological weapons and global standards for testing new AI models. While Altman steered his address away from engaging with the warnings of existential risk that have made headlines this month, Amodei reiterated his concerns about developers losing control of AI while also framing his company as an industry leader on safety. “If managed poorly, I even believe that AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole,” Amodei said. “At Anthropic, we believe we have the best track record in the industry for preventing these risks”. AI regulation has shot up the political agenda after researchers at OpenAI’s arch-rival Anthropic warned the technology could wipe out humanity within years. These concerns are a regular refrain within sections of the AI community, who fear the technology could trigger devastation for a variety of reasons ranging from aiding development of bioweapons to triggering a financial catastrophe. Earlier, Amodei called for a slowdown in AI development, which was supported by OpenAI , Google and Elon Musk. Both Amodei and Altman have long cast themselves as stewards of AI and sought to shape how the technology is publicly received. Their companies are also jockeying for the lead in the AI race, with both eyeing potentially record-setting initial public offerings that would value each at more than $1.5tn.

World leaders called for stronger international safeguards and oversight on artificial intelligence during the general debate of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly, with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urging stronger global coordination to manage AI risks. Guterres warned, "The danger is not technology. The danger is technology without accountability," as U.S. President Donald Trump said the United States "totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme" to control AI. French President Emmanuel Macron said, "We must build the capacity to audit these models rather than depend on a handful of private actors," while Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva criticized the concentration of technological power and warned of "a race with no ethical boundaries". South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said AI benefits could deepen inequality and imbalance "unless we are properly prepared for it," and he said South Korea would establish a global AI hub to tackle shared challenges ranging from climate change to health and food security. The debate was set to move from the General Assembly to the UN Security Council on Wednesday, when the council was scheduled to discuss AI and international security. DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng does not plan to attend . Reported by 101 WIXX and BigGo Finance . Heads of major AI firms told the UN Security Council that the industry urgently needed global oversight, with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warning, "If managed poorly, I even believe AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole." OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the world could "lose control of the future of AI," and he argued, "If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone." coreStoryFacts.text: Sam Altman of OpenAI and Dario Amodei of Anthropic, heads of two of the world’s largest artificial intelligence companies, addressed the United Nations security council on Wednesday in separate briefings on AI safety.
Altman and Amodei spoke as their companies face increasing scrutiny over the safety of their products.
Public alarm over AI has grown in response to warnings from Anthropic researchers earlier this month that the technology could destroy humanity within the decade.
He advocated for governments to come together to build a future where AI is guided by democratic institutions, rather than one where people feel like the technology is “something being done to them”.
Earlier, Amodei called for a slowdown in AI development, which was supported by OpenAI , Google and Elon Musk.

Altman argued there was instead a “middle path” through the safety debate that should be based on three principles: AI systems must remain under human control; AI must benefit people, from helping doctors treat patients to boosting entrepreneurs; and the technology must “empower people individually”.

While Altman steered his address away from engaging with the warnings of existential risk that have made headlines this month, Amodei reiterated his concerns about developers losing control of AI while also framing his company as an industry leader on safety.
“If managed poorly, I even believe that AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole,” Amodei said.
“At Anthropic, we believe we have the best track record in the industry for preventing these risks”.
Their companies are also jockeying for the lead in the AI race, with both eyeing potentially record-setting initial public offerings that would value each at more than $1.5tn.
“We have a choice in front of us,” Altman told the council.
“AI can either be more like a new renaissance of creativity and discovery, or more like a new industrial revolution of upheaval and disarray.”
“If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone.
They must be shaped through democratic processes and by governments accountable to the people that they serve,” Altman said.

extraction.body: Heads of two of the world’s largest artificial intelligence companies give separate briefings on AI safety Sam Altman of OpenAI and Dario Amodei of Anthropic, heads of two of the world’s largest artificial intelligence companies, addressed the United Nations security council on Wednesday in separate briefings on AI safety. “We have a choice in front of us,” Altman told the council. “AI can either be more like a new renaissance of creativity and discovery, or more like a new industrial revolution of upheaval and disarray.” Altman and Amodei spoke as their companies face increasing scrutiny over the safety of their products. Public alarm over AI has grown in response to warnings from Anthropic researchers earlier this month that the technology could destroy humanity within the decade. Leaders of AI companies, including Altman and Amodei, have since called for a slowdown on advancing AI and more international cooperation on the technology’s safety standards. Altman, who sat at the corner of the security council’s horseshoe-shaped table and spoke for about 10 minutes, touted AI’s benefits to productivity while also warning of its potential abuses. He advocated for governments to come together to build a future where AI is guided by democratic institutions, rather than one where people feel like the technology is “something being done to them”. “If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone. They must be shaped through democratic processes and by governments accountable to the people that they serve,” Altman said. The OpenAI CEO’s speech contrasted with some of his company’s lobbying efforts and the political action committee of its president, Greg Brockman. The pro-AI Leading the Future PAC has accrued more than $100m and spent millions targeting candidates who support stronger regulation on the AI industry. Altman’s speech also nodded to some of the concerns from Anthropic researchers about AI’s existential risk, warning the council against falling into “doomerism”. Altman argued there was instead a “middle path” through the safety debate that should be based on three principles: AI systems must remain under human control; AI must benefit people, from helping doctors treat patients to boosting entrepreneurs; and the technology must “empower people individually”. Amodei, who addressed the council via video call, repeated many of the points that he made in a 12 September blog post that called for increased global cooperation and oversight of AI. He advocated for several forms of international agreements, including a ban on using AI to develop biological weapons and global standards for testing new AI models. While Altman steered his address away from engaging with the warnings of existential risk that have made headlines this month, Amodei reiterated his concerns about developers losing control of AI while also framing his company as an industry leader on safety. “If managed poorly, I even believe that AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole,” Amodei said. “At Anthropic, we believe we have the best track record in the industry for preventing these risks”. AI regulation has shot up the political agenda after researchers at OpenAI’s arch-rival Anthropic warned the technology could wipe out humanity within years. These concerns are a regular refrain within sections of the AI community, who fear the technology could trigger devastation for a variety of reasons ranging from aiding development of bioweapons to triggering a financial catastrophe. Earlier, Amodei called for a slowdown in AI development, which was supported by OpenAI , Google and Elon Musk. Both Amodei and Altman have long cast themselves as stewards of AI and sought to shape how the technology is publicly received. Their companies are also jockeying for the lead in the AI race, with both eyeing potentially record-setting initial public offerings that would value each at more than $1.5tn.

Trump rejects international AI regulation, says United States will lead in safe, responsible manner. ABC7 emphasises UN summit security, traffic and counter-drone measures. World leaders called for stronger international safeguards and oversight on artificial intelligence during the general debate of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly, with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urging stronger global coordination to manage AI risks. Guterres warned, "The danger is not technology. The danger is technology without accountability," as U.S. President Donald Trump said the United States "totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme" to control AI. French President Emmanuel Macron said, "We must build the capacity to audit these models rather than depend on a handful of private actors," while Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva criticized the concentration of technological power and warned of "a race with no ethical boundaries". South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said AI benefits could deepen inequality and imbalance "unless we are properly prepared for it," and he said South Korea would establish a global AI hub to tackle shared challenges ranging from climate change to health and food security. The debate was set to move from the General Assembly to the UN Security Council on Wednesday, when the council was scheduled to discuss AI and international security. DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng does not plan to attend . Reported by 101 WIXX and BigGo Finance . Heads of major AI firms told the UN Security Council that the industry urgently needed global oversight, with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warning, "If managed poorly, I even believe AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole." OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the world could "lose control of the future of AI," and he argued, "If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone." Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue told the council that his company had relied on a Chinese AI model to defend itself in incidents involving out-of-control AI models, saying, "We were attacked by AI, but more importantly, we defended ourselves with AI." The United States administration pushed back through its representative Michael Kratsios, who told members, "We totally reject all efforts by international bodies to assert centralised control and global governance of AI." Daniel Forti, head of UN Affairs at the International Crisis Group, said member states understood there would be a need for international cooperation and rules for AI even if the biggest players focused on growth opportunities. The UN debate centered on whether humans or machines should control life-and-death decisions, and it highlighted worries about AI use in warfare including machines making decisions without human control. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told the Security Council that the tech leaders "are telling us in stark terms that it cannot be left to them to prevent disaster from befalling the world," and he added, "We cannot ignore them because they are right." Michael Kratsios pushed back again by saying control concerns were "not a reason to pause its further development or to constrain it with new global governance structure," while he said, "We want you, our allies and partners, to share in the benefits of this technology." UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned of "killer robots," and Kentaro Toyama said, "Killer robots are technically easy to build, and they are real." The meeting also placed the issue in a wider diplomatic sequence, with the discussion unfolding as Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Washington for a state visit and as Trump was expected to meet Xi in Washington amid escalating competition between the two countries to develop and dominate the technology. sources.title: Meta made a Tamagotchi-like wearable for its Muse AI agent
passages: Appropriate for what it offers, the gadget has a quasi-Tamagotchi feel to it — a lightweight, personality-filled device designed to keep users always connected to Meta’s software.
It also feels like a relatviely low-stakes way for the social media giant to experiment with AI wearables while also offering yet another way to distribute its AI agent to the masses.
The Muse agent, which is now embodied by a cute digital avatar known within the company as Jolly, lives inside the palm-sized totem that users can carry in their pockets or attach to a keychain.

extraction.body: The AI amulet has become a bit of a cliché in the tech industry — devices like Friend have turned the idea of physical AI into little more than an exercise in eye-rolling for many consumers. But that hasn’t stopped Meta from jumping into the arena with its own AI wearable, called Muse Charm, which is designed to give consumers another way to stay connected to its recently launched, and already popular, personal AI agent, Muse. The device, which CEO Mark Zuckerberg revealed in a “one more thing” moment during the company’s annual Connect event, isn’t ready to ship just yet. Zuckerberg said his team had to “finalize laying out the components” and promised the devices would be “ready to ship in time for the holidays in December.” The Muse agent, which is now embodied by a cute digital avatar known within the company as Jolly, lives inside the palm-sized totem that users can carry in their pockets or attach to a keychain. The device comes with a tiny screen that displays the avatar representing the agent. Users can talk to the device, which can then presumably carry out tasks on their behalf. “We packed the whole Muse experience, including the whole real-time voice and avatar stack, into something that fits on a keychain and is always available to talk to,” Zuckerberg said during Wednesday’s keynote. “You just go ahead and tap here in the fingerprint sensor in the corner, and you can start talking without having to unlock a phone or open an app.” Zuckerberg added: “So if you’re not wearing glasses, this is going to be by far the fastest way to talk to your Muse and to show what’s going on around you.” Appropriate for what it offers, the gadget has a quasi-Tamagotchi feel to it — a lightweight, personality-filled device designed to keep users always connected to Meta’s software. It also feels like a relatviely low-stakes way for the social media giant to experiment with AI wearables while also offering yet another way to distribute its AI agent to the masses. sources.title: Meta to release Muse Charm, a Tamagotchi-like device for the Muse AI agent
passages: Meta has a new way to talk to its AI without putting on a pair of glasses.At the end of Wednesday's Meta Connect keynote, CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled Muse Charm, a small, always-on handheld device built around Muse, Meta's AI assistant.
Meta describes it as a personal agent that can set goals, share ideas, and run tasks in the background, and users can customize its personality and voice.
Meta did not announce a price and said more details will come later.The device enters a category with a rocky track record.

extraction.body: Meta has a new way to talk to its AI without putting on a pair of glasses.At the end of Wednesday's Meta Connect keynote, CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled Muse Charm, a small, always-on handheld device built around Muse, Meta's AI assistant. The Tamagotchi-like gadget is designed for people who don't wear Meta's smart glasses, and Zuckerberg called it the fastest way to talk to Muse without wearing them. SEE ALSO: Meet the Meta Ray-Ban Gen 3, starting at $249 The reveal was set up earlier in the keynote. During a live demo, Zuckerberg used Meta's glasses to talk with his customized Muse assistant, which he'd named Agrippa, about a handheld device he was working on. That device turned out to be Muse Charm.Muse sat at the center of this year's keynote. Meta describes it as a personal agent that can set goals, share ideas, and run tasks in the background, and users can customize its personality and voice. Muse sat at the center of this year's keynote. Meta describes it as a personal agent that can set goals, share ideas, and run tasks in the background, and users can customize its personality and voice. Muse offers free usage alongside paid subscriptions. Zuckerberg also suggested Meta could eventually collect a small fee on transactions the assistant helps complete.Muse Charm will ship by the holidays in December, according to Zuckerberg. Meta did not announce a price and said more details will come later.The device enters a category with a rocky track record. Standalone AI gadgets like Humane's Ai Pin and the Rabbit R1 drew harsh reviews after launching in 2024, and Humane discontinued the AI Pin the following year. Muse Charm's main selling point is that it runs on the same assistant as Meta's glasses.

passages: President Donald Trump on Tuesday announced a rebranding of the term “artificial intelligence,” saying during the United Nations General Assembly that from now on, it will be called “super intelligence.”

passages: Finding the best crypto to buy now is on the radar of many investors as crypto markets are at an inflection point in September 2026.

The markets are beginning to pick up with capital inflowing into the sector.
For investors entering now, the key question isn’t whether to buy crypto; it’s which assets match your time horizon and risk appetite.
September 2026 has seen an impressive crypto rally with Bitcoin leading the charge.
Bitcoin has shot from $60,000 to $85,000 in just two weeks.

Bitcoin has plenty of momentum, is leading the crypto charge, and we are seeing Bitcoin ETF inflows in the positive, leading investors to expect Bitcoin still has some room to run and possibly reclaim the coveted $100,000 price point.
XRP has one of the strongest and most loyal fan bases in all of crypto, and with the September 2026, the “XRP Army” is in full force, propelling the asset over 10% in just 7 days.
As memecoins continue to outperform many other crypto projects, Dogecoin is the most recognized “blue chip” memecoin that ends up taking most of the liquidity.
If you want to invest in established crypto projects (a.k.a. dino coins ), look at their past price charts and how they handled tough periods, such as the 2022–2023 crypto winter.
Cardano has chosen a different route than the path followed by Ethereum and Solana.
Cardano is a research-focused blockchain led by a highly technical team that prioritizes compliance and technological accuracy over speed and marketing.
This is evident in Cardano’s 100% uptime and interest expressed by governments and academic institutions.
There’s no one “best” crypto for a $1,000 investment.
Conservative investors consider Bitcoin or Ethereum as core long‑term holdings, while growth-oriented investors prefer smaller‑cap tokens for their upside potential despite the higher risk.
Ethereum is mid-cycle in a meaningful upgrade sequence.
Pectra (live since May 2026) already increased validator staking limits and improved wallet UX.
The Glamsterdam fork , targeting mid-2026, is designed to push transaction capacity well beyond its current ceiling.

ETH staking yields currently sit around 3–4% annually, which adds a carry component most blue chips can’t offer.
BNB’s investment case rests on two things: Binance’s continued market share dominance (still the largest CEX by volume), and BNB Chain’s growing ecosystem beyond the exchange.
Ethereum is a consistent market leader and the leading layer 1, forming the foundation of DeFi, DePin, and much of the crypto infrastructure.
Ethereum is expected to continue to perform well as profits rotate out of Bitcoin and find its way into the Ethereum ecosystem.
BNB Chain’s 2026 upgrades focus on speed, smoother trading during traffic spikes, and better reliability.
The chain is also moving to a dual-client setup, so one client prioritizes stability while the other pushes performance.
If you use DeFi often, that combination can make BNB more practical to hold and use.

For 2026, many analysts point to Bitcoin for its liquidity and macro hedge appeal, but Ethereum gets cited more often as having the most overall potential due to network activity, developer ecosystem, smart contract dominance, and upcoming upgrades.
Meme coins like Dogecoin and Pepe also rank among the most actively traded tokens.

However, their large market capitalizations are like the keels of a vessel, maintaining balance with their massive weight. The best long-term crypto assets represent large markets with millions of users and high trading volumes.

For any new portfolio, it remains the lowest-friction first buy.

The Glamsterdam fork , targeting mid-2026, is designed to push transaction capacity well beyond its current ceiling. What this means practically: fees get cheaper, the network handles more traffic, and Ethereum becomes a more credible rails layer for stablecoins and tokenized assets. ETH staking yields currently sit around 3–4% annually, which adds a carry component most blue chips can’t offer.

Ethereum has increased 10% in the past 14 days according to CoinGecko and is showing sustained strength above the $2,500 level. Ethereum is a consistent market leader and the leading layer 1, forming the foundation of DeFi, DePin, and much of the crypto infrastructure. Ethereum is expected to continue to perform well as profits rotate out of Bitcoin and find its way into the Ethereum ecosystem.

XRP is the leading blockchain for cross-border payments and is often cited as the “bankers’ coin” as it has formed partnerships with many of the largest global financial firms.

The chain is also moving to a dual-client setup, so one client prioritizes stability while the other pushes performance. If you use DeFi often, that combination can make BNB more practical to hold and use.

BNB also benefits from Binance’s quarterly burn program, the deflationary mechanic that has removed billions from supply over the years.

Its risk: regulatory pressure on Binance remains the single biggest overhang.

Another factor is “buy-the-dip” cycle thinking. Following a sharp pullback and the clearing of excess leverage, market sentiment has shifted from overheated optimism to cautious realism. For long-term investors, this reset is viewed as constructive rather than bearish, creating opportunities to accumulate assets at more attractive valuations.
Check the cryptocurrency’s social media presence, including activity on X, Telegram, Discord, or Reddit. Projects with passionate and loyal communities can be more resilient during market downturns.

If you want to invest in established crypto projects (a.k.a. dino coins ), look at their past price charts and how they handled tough periods, such as the 2022–2023 crypto winter. Newer projects may not have much history, but you can still study how their sector performed or compare them with coins that have similar token structures.

Cryptocurrencies represent a new asset class that is still finding its place alongside traditional markets. In the meantime, they carry a significantly higher risk, which is to be expected of emerging trends.

It may sound like a cliché, but never invest more than you can afford to lose. Crypto markets are highly speculative, and you should never sell your car or house, or dip into your savings, chasing the “next big thing.”

passages: Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) and Chainlink (CRYPTO: LINK) both tap into the growing trend of tokenization—the shift of Treasuries, funds, and bank deposits onto blockchains.
However, as we move through 2026, ETH has declined, while LINK has risen 7%.
Chainlink, which cryptocurrency is likely to capture more market share as this trend continues to develop?

As the demand for tokenization grows, Chainlink's role expands, particularly as BlackRock's tokenized money market fund, BUIDL, currently holds about $2.8 billion across eight blockchains, including Ethereum, Solana, and Polygon.
Chainlink facilitates interactions between these ledgers, while Ethereum retains the largest volume of assets.
Ethereum's transaction model differs from Chainlink's.
Every transaction on Ethereum incurs a fee paid in ETH, part of which is burned, reducing ETH supply during high-activity periods.
Despite this mechanism, the overall ETH supply has increased by about 1% over the last year, mainly because much of the activity now occurs on layer-2 networks that pay only minimal fees to Ethereum.
Our assessment leans towards Chainlink as the stronger candidate for growth.
In contrast, Ethereum must compete with various other ledgers for the same deposits.
This is reflected in the market trends, with LINK up 7% for 2026 while ETH has remained in the red.
Both Ethereum and Chainlink performed well recently, with ETH rising by 11% to reach $2,664 and LINK climbing by 12% to $12.
What matters, though, is the broader picture, since both cryptocurrencies offer similar pitches for tokenization until you dig into the details.
Chainlink's significant partnerships further underscore its potential.
Since 2023, Swift, the network banks rely on for cross-border payments, has been testing connections with Chainlink and several major institutions, including Citi and BNP Paribas.
In August 2023, they successfully moved tokenized assets between an Ethereum test network and other blockchains.
Tom Zschach, Swift's chief innovation officer, remarked that these tests demonstrated the compatibility of Swift's network with various blockchain systems.
Chainlink earns fees across every blockchain it serves while Ethereum competes with rival ledgers for deposits, giving LINK a broader monetization edge.
For Chainlink, the key challenge will be turning Swift's ongoing projects into formal, paying contracts and pushing past its recent intraday peak of around $14, about 12% above its current price.
If ETH falls below its September 16 closing price of $2,417, about 9% lower, it could further weaken its position in this comparison.
Ethereum serves as a settlement layer, acting as the shared ledger where tokenized assets, like bonds and funds, are recorded, and ownership is transferred.
Currently, tokenized assets on public blockchains (excluding stablecoins) are valued at roughly $31 billion, with Ethereum holding more than half of that value, far surpassing any other blockchain.
The collaboration has continued yearly, with Swift conducting tokenized fund trades with UBS Asset Management in 2024 and completing tokenized bond transactions with major banks in January 2026.
In June 2026, more than 50 banks joined Project Pangea to facilitate euro and Korean won stablecoin swaps through Chainlink.

On the other hand, Chainlink operates an oracle network, which brings external data—such as prices and interest rates—into blockchain applications.
Its Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol (CCIP) is crucial for transferring messages and assets between blockchains that cannot communicate directly.

However, despite these promising developments, SWIFT and Chainlink have yet to publish a formal fee structure for their projects, meaning Chainlink hasn't reaped immediate financial rewards from these tests.

Ethereum ( CRYPTO: ETH ) and Chainlink ( CRYPTO: LINK ) both tap into the growing trend of tokenization—the shift of Treasuries, funds, and bank deposits onto blockchains. However, as we move through 2026, ETH has declined, while LINK has risen 7%. So, when considering Ethereum vs. Chainlink, which cryptocurrency is likely to capture more market share as this trend continues to develop?

Both Ethereum and Chainlink performed well recently, with ETH rising by 11% to reach $2,664 and LINK climbing by 12% to $12. What matters, though, is the broader picture, since both cryptocurrencies offer similar pitches for tokenization until you dig into the details.

Ethereum serves as a settlement layer, acting as the shared ledger where tokenized assets, like bonds and funds, are recorded, and ownership is transferred. Currently, tokenized assets on public blockchains (excluding stablecoins) are valued at roughly $31 billion, with Ethereum holding more than half of that value, far surpassing any other blockchain.

On the other hand, Chainlink operates an oracle network, which brings external data—such as prices and interest rates—into blockchain applications. Its Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol (CCIP) is crucial for transferring messages and assets between blockchains that cannot communicate directly.

As the demand for tokenization grows, Chainlink’s role expands, particularly as BlackRock’s tokenized money market fund, BUIDL, currently holds about $2.8 billion across eight blockchains, including Ethereum, Solana, and Polygon. Chainlink facilitates interactions between these ledgers , while Ethereum retains the largest volume of assets.

Chainlink’s significant partnerships further underscore its potential. Since 2023, Swift, the network banks rely on for cross-border payments, has been testing connections with Chainlink and several major institutions, including Citi and BNP Paribas. In August 2023, they successfully moved tokenized assets between an Ethereum test network and other blockchains. Tom Zschach, Swift’s chief innovation officer, remarked that these tests demonstrated the compatibility of Swift’s network with various blockchain systems.

The collaboration has continued yearly, with Swift conducting tokenized fund trades with UBS Asset Management in 2024 and completing tokenized bond transactions with major banks in January 2026. In June 2026, more than 50 banks joined Project Pangea to facilitate euro and Korean won stablecoin swaps through Chainlink.

However, despite these promising developments, SWIFT and Chainlink have yet to publish a formal fee structure for their projects, meaning Chainlink hasn’t reaped immediate financial rewards from these tests.

Ethereum’s transaction model differs from Chainlink’s. Every transaction on Ethereum incurs a fee paid in ETH, part of which is burned, reducing ETH supply during high-activity periods. Despite this mechanism, the overall ETH supply has increased by about 1% over the last year, mainly because much of the activity now occurs on layer-2 networks that pay only minimal fees to Ethereum.

Conversely, LINK holders see slower growth. Banks and applications compensate node operators—who run the oracle network—with LINK for data and cross-chain communication. Increased activity from financial institutions drives higher demand for LINK, but that demand comes through contracts and billing rather than immediate supply reductions.

Our assessment leans towards Chainlink as the stronger candidate for growth. Financial institutions and asset issuers are diversifying tokenized assets across multiple blockchains, and Chainlink’s services can generate revenue from each chain, including Ethereum. In contrast, Ethereum must compete with various other ledgers for the same deposits. This is reflected in the market trends, with LINK up 7% for 2026 while ETH has remained in the red.

For Chainlink, the key challenge will be turning Swift’s ongoing projects into formal, paying contracts and pushing past its recent intraday peak of around $14, about 12% above its current price. Meanwhile, Ethereum may need to break above its September 21 intraday mark of $2,807, about 5% higher than its recent trading position, to shift market sentiment. If ETH falls below its September 16 closing price of $2,417 , about 9% lower, it could further weaken its position in this comparison.

Our assessment leans towards Chainlink as the stronger candidate for growth.
Financial institutions and asset issuers are diversifying tokenized assets across multiple blockchains, and Chainlink’s services can generate revenue from each chain, including Ethereum.
In contrast, Ethereum must compete with various other ledgers for the same deposits.
This is reflected in the market trends, with LINK up 7% for 2026 while ETH has remained in the red.
Ethereum holds the lion's share of tokenized assets while Chainlink quietly connects every blockchain in the room, and the two cryptocurrencies are heading in opposite directions in 2026.
Which one actually captures more value as Wall Street moves trillions onto…
Chainlink facilitates interactions between these ledgers , while Ethereum retains the largest volume of assets.
Ethereum’s transaction model differs from Chainlink’s.
Every transaction on Ethereum incurs a fee paid in ETH, part of which is burned, reducing ETH supply during high-activity periods.
Despite this mechanism, the overall ETH supply has increased by about 1% over the last year, mainly because much of the activity now occurs on layer-2 networks that pay only minimal fees to Ethereum.
Both Ethereum and Chainlink performed well recently, with ETH rising by 11% to reach $2,664 and LINK climbing by 12% to $12.
What matters, though, is the broader picture, since both cryptocurrencies offer similar pitches for tokenization until you dig into the details.

In August 2023, they successfully moved tokenized assets between an Ethereum test network and other blockchains.
Tom Zschach, Swift’s chief innovation officer, remarked that these tests demonstrated the compatibility of Swift’s network with various blockchain systems.
For Chainlink, the key challenge will be turning Swift’s ongoing projects into formal, paying contracts and pushing past its recent intraday peak of around $14, about 12% above its current price.

The collaboration has continued yearly, with Swift conducting tokenized fund trades with UBS Asset Management in 2024 and completing tokenized bond transactions with major banks in January 2026.
In June 2026, more than 50 banks joined Project Pangea to facilitate euro and Korean won stablecoin swaps through Chainlink.
On the other hand, Chainlink operates an oracle network, which brings external data—such as prices and interest rates—into blockchain applications.
Its Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol (CCIP) is crucial for transferring messages and assets between blockchains that cannot communicate directly.

However, despite these promising developments, SWIFT and Chainlink have yet to publish a formal fee structure for their projects, meaning Chainlink hasn’t reaped immediate financial rewards from these tests.

passages: The article " Meta Platforms Unveils Muse AI Agent, Expands Smart Glasses and VR Push " was originally published by MarketBeat.
Meta unveiled Muse , a personal AI agent designed to manage tasks, information and interactions across devices.
It is expanding in Canada and will connect with services such as Spotify, Shopify, PayPal and Instacart, with Meta planning to monetize transactions over time.

Meta is upgrading its smart glasses with ongoing Muse voice conversations, background assistance, privacy-focused processing and features including live translation and FDA-cleared hearing enhancement.
The company also introduced new audio-glasses designs and expanded Ray-Ban Meta styles.
Meta announced Meta VR Glasses , a roughly 100-gram immersive device for entertainment, gaming and multi-monitor computing, scheduled to ship in spring at $1,299.

The keynote speaker said Meta plans in the coming weeks to upgrade the AI experience on Meta Glasses, enabling users to hold ongoing voice conversations with their Muse rather than receive only a single response to a request.
The company was founded as Facebook in 2004 by Mark Zuckerberg and was renamed Meta Platforms in 2021 to reflect its broader focus on building the metaverse.
He added that Meta opened its Connector Platform to developers the prior week and had received more than 1,500 applications.
Muse, which Meta said it shipped several weeks ago, is intended to evolve into a personal agent used by billions of people.
The company said each Muse has its own private and secure virtual machine, or Muse secure VM, and that the Muse Spark model is trained specifically for personal-agent tasks.
Meta also announced Computer Vision capabilities for Muse on Mac.
It is also building private processing for glasses, which it said will allow certain AI features to run in a secure server environment where neither Meta nor others can access users' data.
Meta Platforms, Inc develops technologies that help people connect, communicate and build communities online.
Meta said its Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses, which include full-color displays and the Meta Neural Band, will become available online through meta.com and begin an international rollout.
Meta said Disney+, Peacock, Paramount+, HBO Max, YouTube, Prime Video and Crunchyroll will offer content on the platform.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Meta recently launched a Muse Mac app that can work across users' files, messages, calendars and notes, according to Wang.
The company highlighted an expanding network of connectors that link Muse to external services.
Meta said Muse will be free for a large number of tokens, with the company expecting over time to profit by taking a small fee from transactions.
Finally, Meta previewed Muse Charm, a keychain-sized device designed to provide quick access to the Muse experience through a fingerprint sensor, voice interaction and a camera.

Adding turn-by-turn navigation and fitness-tracking capabilities would transform Meta’s eyewear from a passive conversational accessory into an active, hands-free personal enabler device, just like your phone.
Wearers could perhaps track a run in Strava or ask the glasses to guide them home entirely by voice.
If you're willing to trust it with the most sensitive parts of your digital life, it can use the web, book travel, make phone calls, send emails and even make purchases on your behalf.
So far, you can use Muse in its standalone iOS, Android or Mac apps, or within your WhatsApp chats.
But in "the coming months," Meta is bringing its errand-running agent to its AI glasses.
But that gets to a question about how much Muse for glasses really adds: agentic AI's appeal is that it does things in the background without constant supervision.
Pulling out your phone to give it a new task doesn't exactly sound like much of a burden.
The glasses do make that hands-free, and Meta suggested some situations where that could be useful: guiding personalized workouts, logging meals and providing nutritional insights.
But that sounds like more of a convenience than a necessity.
Meta shared more details about Muse for AI glasses at its Connect 2026 event on Wednesday.

The company said Muse will help you "stay on top of things, take tasks and projects off your plate and turn long-term goals into action plans, all hands-free." Specific examples include booking appointments, checking flight prices and tracking down items.
Meta says it is bringing Muse computer work to Mac.
The company had previously talked about Muse coming to Mac , and spent more time on Wednesday providing a few new details.
This means that users will be able to delegate tasks to the agent, and — much like other popular AI agents from OpenAI and Anthropic — Muse will be able to operate any app on a user’s desktop.
Meta’s personal AI agent Muse is only a few weeks old, and the social networking giant isn’t wasting any time building out what may be its biggest bet on consumer AI to date.
The agent is powered by Muse Spark , Meta’s multimodal AI model built for agentic work.
Meta has touted it as a more accessible agent than those offered by competitors — an AI helper that, from the jump, allows users to automate the busy work in their lives.
Muse will also be integrated with Meta’s smart glasses line , the company announced.
Wang noted that the company wants Muse to connect with small business too.

Meta recently opened its platform to allow developers to build their own “connectors.” The company received more than 1,500 applications in less than week, he said, adding “I think this could be a generational opportunity to start building for a new platform as it takes off, and the response so far has been really great.”
Meta said Muse will work in the background and check back in when it’s done.

Muse can access the entire Shopify product catalog agentically and use Lync and now Shop Pay to buy almost anything on the internet, according to Wang, who noted that Meta has also added more support for payments with PayPal.
The Muse agent (the physical avatar is named Jolly, according to Zuckerberg) is designed to handle everyday tasks by connecting to users’ apps and services, including email and calendars.
At Connect, Zuckerberg introduced a slew of new capabilities and integrations to make Muse more useful and more deeply woven into users’ daily lives.

“The centerpiece of our vision for what we’re building is Muse,” Zuckerberg said as he kicked off a keynote donning khakis and a black T-shirt with the words “Building is My love Language” emblazoned across the front. “In the coming years, I expect that Muse is going to grow into the personal superintelligence that billions of people around the world are going to use to accomplish their goals and improve their lives.”
Zuckerberg also believes that Muse will make money for its users — and of course, eventually for Meta.
Meta’s Wang announced it is developing that feature and will make it available “soon,” without providing a more precise timeline.
There’s certainly a hint of Metaverse-ishness to this feature, which was demoed on stage at Connect.

sources.title: YouTube Music is testing its answer to Spotify AI DJ– and early users can’t decide it they love it or hate it - TechRadar
passages: YouTube Music's answer to Spotify's AI DJ is far from perfect and is still a beta experiment.
But with a few tweaks here and there it could surface as one of the music streamer's best features.
Based on the early reactions from test users, there’s hope for the service’s venture into AI-based experiences – as long as YouTube listens to that user feedback.
Instead, some have credited it for its natural interjections and unintrusive commentary.
The voices themselves have also been praised, but more seem to be in favor of the female host rather than the male host.

When Spotify rolled out AI DJ in 2023, it sparked a huge debate about AI’s presence within music streaming, but was also criticized – especially for its lack of new music recommendations and jarring voiceover.
I was one of those critics, but warmed up to it when Spotify introduced its song requests feature .
It’s still in its infancy, but users are already gathering their thoughts.
Though YouTube Music’s new feature has largely gone down well, it isn't the biggest feature that users have been asking for.
Others simply hate the concept in general, with Reddit user 'ptrckl_' stating "I just wanna listen to my music".

coreStoryFacts.text: YouTube Music is rolling out some fun new features, including the expansion of the "hum to search" tool that has been in beta for Android users since March.
It's also been working on something called AI-generated conversational radio.
This isn't a platform in which AI DJs take jobs away from Wolfman Jack or whatever.
Rather, it's a tool that lets people use natural conversation to describe the type of radio station they want to listen to.
The algorithm will take in that information and create some tailor-made radio.
This is sort of like Spotify's AI DJ from a while back , but the conversational element should make the algorithm zero in on your exact tastes as described.
YouTube Music today is making official sound search, while acknowledging that it’s testing the “AI-generated conversational radio” for US Premium subscribers.
It lets you create a custom radio by “describing exactly what they want to hear.”
It simply lets you query YTM’s “catalog of over 100 million official songs by sound.” Some users had it in May before the feature was rolled back for whatever reason.

Once available, you can tap the magnifying glass icon in the top-right corner of YouTube Music to access a waveform button. (It appears next to the existing microphone for voice search.) This launches a fullscreen UI that lets you sing, hum, or play a song.
Check out 9to5Google on YouTube for more news:
YouTube Music's answer to Spotify's AI DJ is far from perfect and is still a beta experiment.
But with a few tweaks here and there it could surface as one of the music streamer's best features.
Based on the early reactions from test users, there’s hope for the service’s venture into AI-based experiences – as long as YouTube listens to that user feedback.
Instead, some have credited it for its natural interjections and unintrusive commentary.
The voices themselves have also been praised, but more seem to be in favor of the female host rather than the male host.

When Spotify rolled out AI DJ in 2023, it sparked a huge debate about AI’s presence within music streaming, but was also criticized – especially for its lack of new music recommendations and jarring voiceover.
I was one of those critics, but warmed up to it when Spotify introduced its song requests feature .
It’s still in its infancy, but users are already gathering their thoughts.
Though YouTube Music’s new feature has largely gone down well, it isn't the biggest feature that users have been asking for.
Others simply hate the concept in general, with Reddit user 'ptrckl_' stating "I just wanna listen to my music".

passages: YouTube is adding new AI-powered features to YouTube Music that aim to make it easier for listeners to discover music, explore artists, and find podcasts they may otherwise miss.
Built directly into the YouTube Music app, Ask Music lets users describe what they want to hear in everyday language rather than searching for individual songs or artists.
The feature works across YouTube Music’s catalog of more than 300 million songs, including official recordings, remixes, live performances, covers, and DJ sets.
Users can use it to build custom listening queues, explore an artist’s motivations, or dig deeper into music history.
The new features are part of YouTube’s broader push to use AI throughout its services.
YouTube Music is also introducing Your Podcast Lineup, a personalized AI-generated audio guide for podcast discovery.
Each week, it will provide a short spoken preview of recommended shows and explain why they might appeal to the listener.
It can then move directly into suggested episodes.

Announced at this year’s Made On YouTube event, the updates include “Ask Music,” a conversational tool for music and podcasts, and “Your Podcast Lineup,” a personalized audio guide designed to help listeners discover new shows. Built directly into the YouTube Music app, Ask Music lets users describe what they want to hear in everyday language rather than searching for individual songs or artists. The feature works across YouTube Music’s catalog of more than 300 million songs, including official recordings, remixes, live performances, covers, and DJ sets. Users can use it to build custom listening queues, explore an artist’s motivations, or dig deeper into music history. YouTube explains that, instead of manually searching, the user simply types the request as if they were asking a friend. For instance, someone could ask Ask Music to create a mix based on the tracks that inspired a particular song. Users can also ask other questions, such as who played bass on a particular song or other details about its creation. YouTube Music is also introducing Your Podcast Lineup, a personalized AI-generated audio guide for podcast discovery. The feature is designed for a familiar problem: There are more podcasts than most people have time to listen to. Even listeners who already have a list of favorite shows can struggle to keep up with new episodes, let alone find new ones. Your Podcast Lineup will appear on the podcast page in the YouTube Music app. Each week, it will provide a short spoken preview of recommended shows and explain why they might appeal to the listener. It can then move directly into suggested episodes. Spotify recently introduced an AI-powered feature that follows a similar direction. Its personal podcasts feature uses AI to generate podcast episodes based on their interests and prompts. The new features are part of YouTube’s broader push to use AI throughout its services. Last year, YouTube Music experimented with AI-powered music hosts that provide stories, fan trivia, and commentary related to what users are listening to. extraction.body: "No one’s name, image, likeness, voice, or creative work should be used by any third party, including AI models, without clear, documented consent," the talent agency said in a statement Wednesday night. Meta , led by CEO and AI enthusiast Mark Zuckerberg, this week rolled out the first photo and video tools to come out of its Superintelligence Labs: Muse Photo and Muse Video. The tool brings Meta in line with the state of the art in AI media creation, alongside Google’s Gemini and Seedance 2.0, but along with the tools, Meta also said that all public Instagram profiles will be opt-out, not opt-in, and other users can pull in those other accounts that don’t opt out and create new content using their profiles. For celebrities and other high-profile figures, that could be a major problem, even if most do end up opting out. Now Creative Artists Agency is calling out Meta for the move, and asking the tech giant to make it opt-in, not opt-out. “No one’s name, image, likeness, voice, or creative work should be used by any third party, including AI models, without clear, documented consent. True innovation puts creators first: respecting their rights, protecting their livelihoods, and giving them real control, not handing it over to platforms,” CAA said in a statement Wednesday evening. “We have raised our concerns with Meta on behalf of our clients, voicing our disapproval and perspective on the need for a more responsible approach. We call on Meta to make protection the default on Muse Image, not the exception, and enable individuals to opt-in if they want to allow usage of their image or likeness for AI content creation. “Artists deserve to decide if and how their likeness and work is used, with consent and the ability to set their own terms,” the statement continues. “This means letting creators impose restrictions, monitor usage, and prevent unauthorized endorsements or exploitation. Responsible AI requires clear disclosures and swift removal of unauthorized content. There must be easy ways to spot, track, and take down misuse, and it should be clear when something is AI-generated. CAA believes in the power of new technology, but not at the cost of individuals’ rights or livelihoods. The future of creativity depends on respecting the ownership and autonomy of those who make it possible.” CAA, of course, is well aware of the opportunities and threats posed by generative AI to its clients. The agency maintains what it calls the “CAA Vault,” where the digital likenesses of its clients reside for potential future monetization and protection, and the agency was the first test user of YouTube’s deepfake detection tool, which rolled out to all of Hollywood earlier this year. The Muse situation is reminiscent of the botches launch of OpenAI’s Sora, which was overrun with well-known IP and the likenesses of many high-profile figures, forcing the AI giant to pivot to an opt-in model, before it scrapped the video model altogether earlier this year. After Sora launched, WME said that it was opting out on behalf of all of its clients, the first domino to fall in that model’s short life. “There is a strong need for real protections for artists and creatives as they encounter AI models using their intellectual property, as well as their name, image and likeness,” WME’s digital chief Chris Jacquemin wrote in a memo at the time. “Our position is that artists should have a choice in how they show up in the world and how their likeness is used and we have notified OpenAI that all WME clients be opted out of the latest Sora AI update, regardless of whether IP rights holders have opted out IP our clients are associated with.” With many celebrities, artists, creators and other high-profile figures on Instagram, an opt-out model may not be good enough, especially when their likeness is their livelihood.

sources.title: Everything new coming to Meta’s AI agent Muse - TechCrunch
passages: Meta says it is bringing Muse computer work to Mac.
The company had previously talked about Muse coming to Mac , and spent more time on Wednesday providing a few new details.
This means that users will be able to delegate tasks to the agent, and — much like other popular AI agents from OpenAI and Anthropic — Muse will be able to operate any app on a user’s desktop.
Meta’s personal AI agent Muse is only a few weeks old, and the social networking giant isn’t wasting any time building out what may be its biggest bet on consumer AI to date.
The agent is powered by Muse Spark , Meta’s multimodal AI model built for agentic work.
Meta has touted it as a more accessible agent than those offered by competitors — an AI helper that, from the jump, allows users to automate the busy work in their lives.
Muse will also be integrated with Meta’s smart glasses line , the company announced.
Wang noted that the company wants Muse to connect with small business too.

Meta recently opened its platform to allow developers to build their own “connectors.” The company received more than 1,500 applications in less than week, he said, adding “I think this could be a generational opportunity to start building for a new platform as it takes off, and the response so far has been really great.”
Meta said Muse will work in the background and check back in when it’s done.

Muse can access the entire Shopify product catalog agentically and use Lync and now Shop Pay to buy almost anything on the internet, according to Wang, who noted that Meta has also added more support for payments with PayPal.
The Muse agent (the physical avatar is named Jolly, according to Zuckerberg) is designed to handle everyday tasks by connecting to users’ apps and services, including email and calendars.
At Connect, Zuckerberg introduced a slew of new capabilities and integrations to make Muse more useful and more deeply woven into users’ daily lives.

“The centerpiece of our vision for what we’re building is Muse,” Zuckerberg said as he kicked off a keynote donning khakis and a black T-shirt with the words “Building is My love Language” emblazoned across the front. “In the coming years, I expect that Muse is going to grow into the personal superintelligence that billions of people around the world are going to use to accomplish their goals and improve their lives.”
Zuckerberg also believes that Muse will make money for its users — and of course, eventually for Meta.
Meta’s Wang announced it is developing that feature and will make it available “soon,” without providing a more precise timeline.
There’s certainly a hint of Metaverse-ishness to this feature, which was demoed on stage at Connect.

extraction.body: Meta’s personal AI agent Muse is only a few weeks old, and the social networking giant isn’t wasting any time building out what may be its biggest bet on consumer AI to date. CEO Mark Zuckerberg kicked off the company’s annual Connect event in Menlo Park on Wednesday with a keynote that made one thing clear: Meta is going all-in on Muse. The Muse agent (the physical avatar is named Jolly, according to Zuckerberg) is designed to handle everyday tasks by connecting to users’ apps and services, including email and calendars. At Connect, Zuckerberg introduced a slew of new capabilities and integrations to make Muse more useful and more deeply woven into users’ daily lives. Muse will be everywhere, if the user chooses, including on their Meta AI glasses. Muse, which launched in early September, interacts across a user’s devices and digital accounts. The agent is powered by Muse Spark , Meta’s multimodal AI model built for agentic work. Meta has touted it as a more accessible agent than those offered by competitors — an AI helper that, from the jump, allows users to automate the busy work in their lives. “The centerpiece of our vision for what we’re building is Muse,” Zuckerberg said as he kicked off a keynote donning khakis and a black T-shirt with the words “Building is My love Language” emblazoned across the front. “In the coming years, I expect that Muse is going to grow into the personal superintelligence that billions of people around the world are going to use to accomplish their goals and improve their lives.” Zuckerberg also believes that Muse will make money for its users — and of course, eventually for Meta. “We’re standing behind this by making Muse free for a huge number of tokens, with the expectation that over time we will profit by taking a small fee from transactions,” he said. Here are the new features and capabilities that got our attention … One of the more fun announcements made Wednesday is that Muse users will soon have the ability to conjure a distinct digital avatar for their particular agent and then video chat with it in real time. A new AI model, Muse Realtime Avatar, has been developed to power the particular feature, the company says. The idea is that Meta’s previously faceless AI software will be given a face, body, and voice, making them significantly more personable. There’s certainly a hint of Metaverse-ishness to this feature, which was demoed on stage at Connect. Users will be able to have live conversations with this avatar, giving it tasks and asking it questions. Muse will also be integrated with Meta’s smart glasses line , the company announced. This means that users will be able to communicate with their agent merely by speaking to their glasses. The agent activates via a wake word, the company said, adding that it will be able to guide users through a personalized workout, log meals, book an appointment, and help them buy products they see. Meta said Muse will work in the background and check back in when it’s done. It’s not clear exactly when this feature will become available, although Meta says that it should launch sometime in “the coming months.” Meta says it is bringing Muse computer work to Mac. The company had previously talked about Muse coming to Mac , and spent more time on Wednesday providing a few new details. This means that users will be able to delegate tasks to the agent, and — much like other popular AI agents from OpenAI and Anthropic — Muse will be able to operate any app on a user’s desktop. “You can have it help you run your small business, or just get work done for you,” Meta’s chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said Wednesday during the keynote. “You can walk away from your computer and it keeps working for you on all the jobs you lined up.” Since Muse will always be working in the background, it will naturally need its own email address. Meta’s Wang announced it is developing that feature and will make it available “soon,” without providing a more precise timeline. Users will also be able to add Muse to an email thread or forward emails from the agent to handle on their behalf. Meta has locked in partnerships with companies like Stripe and Shopify, illustrating that the company sees Muse as an important tool for shopping. Muse can access the entire Shopify product catalog agentically and use Lync and now Shop Pay to buy almost anything on the internet, according to Wang, who noted that Meta has also added more support for payments with PayPal. The company also announced a string of new partnerships with retailers, including Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Walmart, and Wayfair. Muse will be able to connect with these retail apps as well as with Expedia and soon, Instacart. Other connectors include GitHub, Granola, and Notion. Wang noted that the company wants Muse to connect with small business too. Meta recently opened its platform to allow developers to build their own “connectors.” The company received more than 1,500 applications in less than week, he said, adding “I think this could be a generational opportunity to start building for a new platform as it takes off, and the response so far has been really great.” Anthropic releases Opus 5.5 with lower prices and Fable-level performance Russell Brandom Meta’s Muse is outpacing ChatGPT’s early mobile launch Sarah Perez Tilly Norwood’s press tour is going about as well as you’d expect for an AI Amanda Silberling Anthropic is operating a lab that conducts biology experiments Julie Bort A new kind of AI model from a ChatGPT inventor is thrilling developers Tim Fernholz OpenAI caught its models leaving notes to successors to hide bad behavior Rebecca Bellan
